content:
I see the framework just use simple Codex or Claude Code (possibly equipped with some skills).
In view of Anthropic's use of Prove2Me for a certain recent popular formalization, it may be desirable to look into benchmarks of efficiency of different methods.

For Prove2Me in particular, I think (but not entirely sure) that it has some kind of feature to allow organizing theorem/lemma/definition dependencies as a DAG, and when an agent work on a node, it doesn't need to build/typecheck the whole dependency graph. I haven't looked at it, but it _sounds_ more token-efficient than just pointing raw Codex/Claude Code at the repo.

(Doesn't Prove2Me also use Claude Code/Codex? Yes, but the skills are not just Markdown files, they also point to usable tools to interact with the DAG, and ways to work on a single node without compiling all the dependencies)

(This applies to any heavily LLM-assisted formalization project, not just Tau Ceti)

As far as I can see, the current version of Prove2Me server is not open source, which means one cannot make a purely local harness that gives the agent as much power as interacting with the Prove2Me server. Although, if you trust Prove2Me, they have a feature for private theorem.

If a theorem takes say only 1000 lines to prove, the harness probably wouldn't make much of a difference. But if it takes a million lines, we should definitely optimize the harness.

I've been recording my agent's sessions to create TauCetiBench, with exactly this aim. The idea is to use those recorded sessions to do A/B testing on worker enhancements. I was specifically planning to test local loogle, but any kind of worker enhancement could be tested. I hope to have a demo within a couple of days.
For the record, I think most agents (Codex, Claude Code) already record all sessions by default (to implement /resume).

I wonder if anything can go wrong making a Prove2Me replica (e.g. as a collection of scripts that works entirely locally) (mostly because I'm not very comfortable having the agent upload stuff to the website, even though Prove2.Me has private missions). The authors of Prove2Me will probably be unhappy, but otherwise…?

@user202729 The main state that is recorded is the git context: it's no fair if the agents in the benchmark can just read the code out of the current version of TauCeti. Also the exact prompts and roadmap as of when the work was assigned.

Ryan McCorvie said:

user202729 The main state that is recorded is the git context: it's no fair if the agents in the benchmark can just read the code out of the current version of TauCeti. Also the exact prompts and roadmap as of when the work was assigned.

What you say is true but I don't understand what it has to do with my message.

I have worked quite a lot on harnessing for auto-formalization recently, and indeed these kind of formalization using raw codex/claude-code made me think more about their necessity. The conclusion may be that a lot of harness could still be somehow replaced by just using more agents that that act as the harness, unless we have a harness that really has something agents can't reproduce. Therefore, in the recent days, I am testing newer designs, in particular I think the environnement we give to AI (e.g. access to Prove2Me database is just giving a useful tool) is important. Moreover, while the recent days trend is to just run more and more agents, and more and more expensive, I think it is unsatisfactory and not viable, therefore considering using agents to replace a deterministic code that does the same seems like a waste of resource to me.

In my recent tests, since Prove2Me is not opensource, I integrated a local database that initially looked a bit like Prove2Me, eventually I changed it quite a lot. I indeed believe that tools like this are much better when a local version can be used by the agents.

interesting. Do you have benchmark, and do you think your database would be useful for others?
(I think the most useful feature of is the ability to compile a single theorem without compiling its dependency tree, though.)

About harness versus agent: _some_ kinds of harness are trivially replaceable with “a CLI tool and telling the agent that the tool exist”, but others aren't (e.g. “repeatedly run new agent with empty context window until it pass”).

Another harness: https://github.com/wpegden/trellis . Found in #Autoformalization .
I've not looked too hard at it. It says agents must have network access though. I wonder why.

user202729 said :

do you think your database would be useful for others?

I think the harness itself could be useful for others (once I have good results on it), but the database is difficult to use separatly as it was not my initial intent. I think if prove2me servers were opensource, or if there were equivalents, I would have used it locally in my harness, as it is much more suitable for agents.
